subject: Renewal discussion: proposed staircase commit & rate-band refinement
messages:
From: Sandra Li <sandra@clearway.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom@clearway.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — spike support + rate-limit concerns

Markus,

We’re approaching our seasonal renewal window (Mar 1) and the team wants to lock in a plan that covers predictable monthly throughput while giving us headroom for short bursts. Q4 showed a 3x daily peak on marketing campaigns and the current hosted tier throttled some routes — we need a cleaner commit model to avoid tail latency during spikes.

Can you share what a staircase/step-up commit looks like from Redwood (monthly committed units + burst pool)? Also: how do rate-bands apply at the per-route vs account level? Our SREs are worried about per-route throttling for ingestion pipelines.

Attached: clearway_usage_q4.csv (usage by route).

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

—Sandra
CTO, Clearway Analytics
[attachment: clearway_usage_q4.csv (csv, 42KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Li <sandra@clearway.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom@clearway.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Jan 2028 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — spike support + rate-limit concerns

Sandra — thanks for the usage file, that was super helpful. I pulled a quick analysis with the team and sketched a proposal. High level:

- Proposal: 3-tier staircase commit over 12 months (Base / Mid / Peak) with an aligned monthly credit ladder. Base covers steady-state; Mid unlocks a higher rate-band and larger KV/cache allocations; Peak adds a burst pool (shared) with explicit burst-window hours for campaign days.
- Rate-bands: we can map rate-bands to per-route thresholds (ingest routes get a dedicated route-band) while keeping a global account-level pool for cross-route bursts.
- Fallbacks: when a route hits a per-route limit, we can route selected traffic to a compatible, cheaper model variant for non-critical queries — keeps latency predictable.

I attached a one-page draft amendment and an ops diagram showing burst-window mechanics. If this structure looks reasonable we can:

1) Finalize the commit ladder and monthly $/token math (SalesOps + Pricing)
2) Add the per-route banding into the amendment as a scoped appendix
3) Schedule a 30-min technical sync with your SREs to validate the traffic shaping rules and model fallbacks

Proposed next step: I’ll follow up with a written mutual action plan and a cost matrix for your review. Can Naomi and Karthik look at the pricing/throughput numbers early tomorrow?

Thanks,
Markus
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: mk_proposed_amendment_v1.pdf (pdf, 86KB)]

From: Tom Reyes <tom@clearway.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sandra Li <sandra@clearway.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 08:53:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — spike support + rate-limit concerns

Markus — quick follow-up from our infra team after looking at the draft: a few clarif points before we schedule the SRE sync:

- Can the per-route band be enforced at the API gateway so we get early rejection (400) instead of queueing inside runtime? That helps our observability.
- For the burst pool, what’s the exhaustion policy? Does the system gate down to soft-throttle or hard-reject?
- If we accept model fallback for non-critical queries, how configurable is the failover (we need route-level policies not global only).

Happy to do the 30-min SRE session once we get those answered. Also — the attached traffic profile shows two consistent campaign windows (first week of each month); we'd want guaranteed burst capacity during those windows.

Cheers,
Tom
Head of Platform Engineering, Clearway
[attachment: clearway_traffic_profile.png (png, 120KB)]

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jan 2028 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Renewal planning — need pricing/ops sign-off and AMP

Naomi/Karthik — forwarding Clearway thread. Quick ask: can SalesOps and Pricing validate a 12-month staircase commit priced as below and confirm whether the burst-window guarantee requires a separate SLA addendum? Suggested numbers (ballpark):

- Base: 1.2M tokens / month at $0.0032/token
- Mid: +1.8M tokens / month (when Mid unlocked) at effective $0.0029/token
- Peak: additional shared burst pool 2.0M tokens with 48-hours/month reserved burst-window (applied only to named campaign windows)
- Early-sign bonus: 4% committed discount if signed by Feb 5

Operational asks:
- Implement per-route rate-banding enforced at the Gateway layer with 429s as the default soft-reject; allow a configurable early-reject option (400) if Clearway enables it.
- Define exhaustion behavior: Soft-throttle first (queue/backpressure) then failover to fallback model variants. If burst pool exhausted, hard-reject only for non-fallbackable routes.

Can you both confirm these numbers and any operational caveats? I want to send a formal Mutual Action Plan (AMP) with these line items to Clearway by EOD tomorrow.

—Markus

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Sandra Li <sandra@clearway.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom@clearway.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Jan 2028 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion: proposed staircase commit & rate-band refinement

Sandra / Tom — thanks for the quick turn. Naomi and Karthik confirmed the numbers and ops model; I’ve incorporated your asks into the AMP and attached the redline for review. Key takeaways: 

- Commitment ladder (12-month): Base 1.2M /mo, Mid +1.8M, Peak shared burst 2.0M (48 reserved burst-hours/month)
- Gateway-enforced per-route banding is available. Default behavior: 429 soft-reject; Clearway can opt-in to 400 early-reject for ingest routes during campaigns.
- Exhaustion policy: soft-throttle + fallback to cheaper variants where configured; hard-reject only for explicitly marked non-fallback routes.
- Commercial: effective blended rate shown in attached matrix; 4% early-sign incentive if executed by Feb 5.

If this matches your expectations, I’ll prepare the amendment for signature (DocuSign link included) and book the 30-min SRE technical sync (please propose two slots next week).

Action items:
- Sandra/Tom: confirm acceptance of burst-hours and early-sign incentive by Jan 25
- Clearway SREs: provide two 30-min slots for technical sync
- Redwood SalesOps: finalize the amendment and enable gateway-rule config for Clearway account (Naomi/Karthik)

Thanks — attaching: redline of amendment + cost matrix.

Best,
Markus Klein
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
